vulnerabilities.title: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/crypto/tls](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls) is a Go standard library package std/crypto/tls Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
When `Conn.Handshake` fails during ALPN negotiation, the error contains attacker-controlled information (the ALPN protocols sent by the client), which is not escaped. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/tls` to version 1.24.8, 1.25.2 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-4008) - [Go Code Review](https://go.dev/cl/707776) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/75652) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/4Emdl2iQ_bI)

vulnerabilities.title: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/crypto/tls](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls) is a Go standard library package std/crypto/tls Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
During the TLS 1.3 handshake if multiple messages are sent in records that span encryption level boundaries (for instance the Client Hello and Encrypted Extensions messages), the subsequent messages may be processed before the encryption level changes. This can cause some minor information disclosure if a network-local attacker can inject messages during the handshake. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/tls` to version 1.24.12, 1.25.6 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4340) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/724120) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/76443) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/Vd2tYVM8eUc)
vulnerabilities.name: std/crypto/tls

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Certificate Validation
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/crypto/tls](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls) is a Go standard library package std/crypto/tls Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Certificate Validation.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
During session resumption in crypto/tls, if the underlying Config has its ClientCAs or RootCAs fields mutated between the initial handshake and the resumed handshake, the resumed handshake may succeed when it should have failed. This may happen when a user calls `Config.Clone` and mutates the returned Config, or uses `Config.GetConfigForClient`. This can cause a client to resume a session with a server that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake, or cause a server to resume a session with a client that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/tls` to version 1.24.13, 1.25.7, 1.26.0-rc.3 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4337) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/737700) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/77217) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/K09ubi9FQFk)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/crypto/tls](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls) is a Go standard library package std/crypto/tls Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/tls` to version 1.25.9, 1.26.2 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4870) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/763767) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/78334) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU)

## Overview [std/crypto/x509](None) is a Go standard library package std/crypto/x509 Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Certificate Validation.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
An excluded subdomain constraint in a certificate chain does not restrict the usage of wildcard SANs in the leaf certificate. For example a constraint that excludes the subdomain test.example.com does not prevent a leaf certificate from claiming the SAN *.example.com. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/x509` to version 1.24.11, 1.25.5 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-4175) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/723900) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/76442) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/8FJoBkPddm4)

This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/x509` to version 1.25.9, 1.26.2 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4946) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/758061) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/78281) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU)

During chain building, the amount of work that is done is not correctly limited when a large number of intermediate certificates are passed in VerifyOptions.Intermediates, which can lead to a denial of service. This affects both direct users of crypto/x509 and users of crypto/tls. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/x509` to version 1.25.9, 1.26.2 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4947) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/758320) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/78282) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/crypto/x509](None) is a Go standard library package std/crypto/x509 Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
(*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/crypto/x509` to version 1.25.11, 1.26.4 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5037) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/783621) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/79694) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw)

vulnerabilities.title: Race Condition
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/database/sql](https://pkg.go.dev/database/sql) is a Go standard library package std/database/sql Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Race Condition.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
Cancelling a query (e.g. by cancelling the context passed to one of the query methods) during a call to the Scan method of the returned Rows can result in unexpected results if other queries are being made in parallel. This can result in a race condition that may overwrite the expected results with those of another query, causing the call to Scan to return either unexpected results from the other query or an error. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/database/sql` to version 1.23.12, 1.24.6 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-3849) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/693735) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/74831) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/x5MKroML2yM)

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/net/url](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url) is a Go standard library package std/net/url Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
The Parse function permits values other than IPv6 addresses to be included in square brackets within the host component of a URL. RFC 3986 permits IPv6 addresses to be included within the host component, enclosed within square brackets. For example: "http://[::1]/". IPv4 addresses and hostnames must not appear within square brackets. Parse did not enforce this requirement. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/net/url` to version 1.24.8, 1.25.2 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-4010) - [Go Code Review](https://go.dev/cl/709857) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/75678) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/4Emdl2iQ_bI)

## Overview [std/net/url](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url) is a Go standard library package std/net/url Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
The net/url package does not set a limit on the number of query parameters in a query. While the maximum size of query parameters in URLs is generally limited by the maximum request header size, the net/http.Request.ParseForm method can parse large URL-encoded forms. Parsing a large form containing many unique query parameters can cause excessive memory consumption. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/net/url` to version 1.24.12, 1.25.6 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4341) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/736712) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/77101) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/Vd2tYVM8eUc)

vulnerabilities.title: Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[std/net/url](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url) is a Go standard library package std/net/url

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to insufficient validation of the `url.Parse` process. An attacker can bypass expected URL parsing restrictions by supplying specially crafted URLs containing invalid host or authority components.
## Remediation
Upgrade `std/net/url` to version 1.25.8, 1.26.1 or higher.
## References

- [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/77578)

vulnerabilities.title: Symlink Attack
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/os](https://pkg.go.dev/os) is a Go standard library package std/os Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Symlink Attack.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|O_EXCL) behaved differently on Unix and Windows systems when the target path was a dangling symlink. On Unix systems, OpenFile with O_CREATE and O_EXCL flags never follows symlinks. On Windows, when the target path was a symlink to a nonexistent location, OpenFile would create a file in that location. OpenFile now always returns an error when the O_CREATE and O_EXCL flags are both set and the target path is a symlink. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/os` to version 1.23.10, 1.24.4 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-3750) - [Go Code Review](https://go.dev/cl/672396) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/73702) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/ufZ8WpEsA3A)
vulnerabilities.name: std/os

vulnerabilities.title: Relative Path Traversal
credit: Dan Sebastian Thrane of SDU eScience Center
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/os](https://pkg.go.dev/os) is a Go standard library package std/os Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Relative Path Traversal.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
It was possible to improperly access the parent directory of an `os.Root` by opening a filename ending in "../". For example, Root.Open("../") would open the parent directory of the Root. This escape only permits opening the parent directory itself, not ancestors of the parent or files contained within the parent. ## Remediation Upgrade `std/os` to version 1.23.9, 1.24.3 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4403) - [Go Commit](https://go.dev/cl/670036) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/73555) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/UZoIkUT367A/m/5WDxKizJAQAJ)
vulnerabilities.name: std/os

vulnerabilities.title: Directory Traversal
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview [std/os](https://pkg.go.dev/os) is a Go standard library package std/os Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Directory Traversal.

**Go Vulnerability Report:**
On Unix platforms, when listing the contents of a directory using File.ReadDir or File.Readdir the returned FileInfo could reference a file outside of the Root in which the File was opened.The impact of this escape is limited to reading metadata provided by lstat from arbitrary locations on the filesystem without permitting reading or writing files outside the root. ## Details A Directory Traversal attack (also known as path traversal) aims to access files and directories that are stored outside the intended folder. By manipulating files with "dot-dot-slash (../)" sequences and its variations, or by using absolute file paths, it may be possible to access arbitrary files and directories stored on file system, including application source code, configuration, and other critical system files. Directory Traversal vulnerabilities can be generally divided into two types: - **Information Disclosure**: Allows the attacker to gain information about the folder structure or read the contents of sensitive files on the system. `st` is a module for serving static files on web pages, and contains a [vulnerability of this type](https://snyk.io/vuln/npm:st:20140206). In our example, we will serve files from the `public` route. If an attacker requests the following URL from our server, it will in turn leak the sensitive private key of the root user. ``` curl http://localhost:8080/public/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/root/.ssh/id_rsa ``` **Note** `%2e` is the URL encoded version of `.` (dot). - **Writing arbitrary files**: Allows the attacker to create or replace existing files. This type of vulnerability is also known as `Zip-Slip`. One way to achieve this is by using a malicious `zip` archive that holds path traversal filenames. When each filename in the zip archive gets concatenated to the target extraction folder, without validation, the final path ends up outside of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily. The following is an example of a `zip` archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicious file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file: ``` 2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt 2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys ``` ## Remediation Upgrade `std/os` to version 1.25.8, 1.26.1 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4602) - [Go Code Review](https://go.dev/cl/749480) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/77827) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/EdhZqrQ98hk#CVE-2026-27139)

On Unix platforms, when listing the contents of a directory using File.ReadDir or File.Readdir the returned FileInfo could reference a file outside of the Root in which the File was opened.The impact of this escape is limited to reading metadata provided by lstat from arbitrary locations on the filesystem without permitting reading or writing files outside the root. ## Details A Directory Traversal attack (also known as path traversal) aims to access files and directories that are stored outside the intended folder. By manipulating files with "dot-dot-slash (../)" sequences and its variations, or by using absolute file paths, it may be possible to access arbitrary files and directories stored on file system, including application source code, configuration, and other critical system files. Directory Traversal vulnerabilities can be generally divided into two types: - **Information Disclosure**: Allows the attacker to gain information about the folder structure or read the contents of sensitive files on the system. `st` is a module for serving static files on web pages, and contains a [vulnerability of this type](https://snyk.io/vuln/npm:st:20140206). In our example, we will serve files from the `public` route. If an attacker requests the following URL from our server, it will in turn leak the sensitive private key of the root user. ``` curl http://localhost:8080/public/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/root/.ssh/id_rsa ``` **Note** `%2e` is the URL encoded version of `.` (dot). - **Writing arbitrary files**: Allows the attacker to create or replace existing files. This type of vulnerability is also known as `Zip-Slip`. One way to achieve this is by using a malicious `zip` archive that holds path traversal filenames. When each filename in the zip archive gets concatenated to the target extraction folder, without validation, the final path ends up outside of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily. The following is an example of a `zip` archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicious file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file: ``` 2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt 2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys ``` ## Remediation Upgrade `std/os` to version 1.25.8, 1.26.1 or higher. ## References - [Go Advisory](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4602) - [Go Code Review](https://go.dev/cl/749480) - [Go Issue](https://go.dev/issue/77827) - [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/EdhZqrQ98hk#CVE-2026-27139)
